correctness.rationale: Full-table additive kernel plus the Woodbury formula yields exact deleted-design rows. Three row orbits are exhaustively classified. U negative mass is (n-2)/n+(n-2)/(nT); B has (n-2)/n; M differs from U by a positive sum-of-squares numerator divided by n(n-2)T, for every integer n>=3 and 0<=r<=n where its orbit exists. These prove global norm, equality rows, strict decrements and [0,1] defect. Independent exact rational 22-design tests across n=3..6 reproduce every row without using the Woodbury row formula. Remaining limit: finite computations alone would not prove the universal sign analysis.

value.rationale: Two-way additive least-squares fitting on an incomplete square table is a natural finite-dimensional approximation problem. The exact worst-case observed-cell sup-norm amplification is not a leverage diagonal. The complete matching-deletion family has a sharp, nontrivial monotonicity law and a final-cell decrement amplified by exactly (n+1)(n-2) over the previous one; all norming cells and sharp positivity loss are classified, providing structural operator information beyond routine numerical examples.
